biggest_gap.title: Edit and save still ties Odoo on keystrokes: Odoo's shortest path takes the same compact number, so it is 3 steps and 14 keys against ours' 2 steps and 14 keys
biggest_gap.detail:
The new phone field and the completed-entry save remove the save key and a step, so ours now wins steps, machine seconds and modelled seconds. Keystrokes still tie. Ours' credited path types +971505550199 (14 keys); the instrument requires +971 to be typed. Odoo's real expert path types the same 14 keys: triple-click the phone field, type +971505550199, click Save. Odoo shows '+971 50 555 0199' on the form, stores '+971505550199', and the instrument credits that entry ('separators free').

The harness misses this for two reasons. The Odoo driver types the spaced number and its verify() demands the exact spaced string, which is stricter than the instrument's own rule. And the instrument still cannot express a triple-click. A tie is a loss, and editing a field is the most frequent action every later module will build on this form.

The digits themselves cannot be cut, so ours needs a credited path that is strictly shorter in keys. The clearest one: ours already supplies +971, so the person types only the 9-digit national number (505550199, 9 keys), and ours stores the full international number. Odoo's 9-digit entry stores just '505550199', without the country code, so Odoo cannot be credited for it, and Odoo stays at 14. For that path to count, the measuring instrument must accept a fixed prefix that a field shows as its own, before the clock, as not needing to be typed. That decision belongs to p01 and the lead; ours' driver comment already describes the 9-digit path. A product alternative is any entry ours can do in fewer keys than 14 that the instrument credits.
